correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and real nonzero w, sign flips reduce to nonnegative b_i. Radius-r feasibility of all coordinate center intervals [M_i-r,m_i+r] intersecting b·c=0 holds iff r>=D/2, r>=sum b_i M_i/W and r>=-sum b_i m_i/W. Choosing a coordinate attaining max b_i and approaching its supremum/infimum gives r<=max{1/2,1-b_max/W}D; the explicit n-point witness 0,e_i-(b_i/b_j)e_j attains the upper bound including zero weights. I independently compared exact formulas against independent linear-programming centers for four weighted cases. The equal-weight n>=3 and dominant coefficient isometry boundaries follow without assumption of positive b_i. Radius normalization r/D (not 2r/D) carefully preserved.
